patch_description: The current implementation runs a pure-Python double loop in `balanced_packing` (over every layer × every expert), making the balancer itself the bottleneck. The new approach keeps the same overall problem decomposition (node packing → replication → GPU packing) but replaces all per-layer Python loops with fully vectorized tensor operations that process all layers simultaneously. Balanced packing is done as a vectorized LPT (longest-processing-time-first) greedy: items are visited in globally sorted order, and for each position the destination pack is chosen with a single masked `argmin` across all layers at once. Replication is a vectorized water-filling greedy on `weight/cnt` (already minimizing the max replica load, which directly improves expert-level balancedness). Everything stays on the GPU (no `.cpu()` round-trips), which removes the host-device sync cost that dominated the original runtime. The result is the same or better packing quality with dramatically lower algorithm execution time.
